structure: Part 10, Commodity lines and animal identification, read the two detail pages of the live-animals commodities feature in trade-imports-animals-frontend and everything they are built from, leaving the search and selection pages to part 9. Read in full: features/commodities/consignment-details/ (consignment-details.controller.js, fields.js, consignment-details.njk, _selected-commodities-table.njk, _species-quantities.njk, view-model/groups.js, view-model/selected-rows.js, view-model/values.js, validation/count-drop.js, remove/actions.js, remove/post-remove.js — skipping the three *.test.js unit tests); features/commodities/animal-identification/ (animal-identification.controller.js, animal-identification.njk, _identification-card.njk, _saved-animals-table.njk, _selected-commodities-summary.njk, animal-label.js, fields.js, line-cap.js, units-for-commodity-line.js, identified-animals.js, card/view-model.js, card/error-summary.js, identifier/fields.js, identifier/table.js, form/forms.js, records/append.js, remove/post-remove.js, summary/selected-commodities.js — skipping its two *.test.js files); the feature-level page.js, lines.js, species-label.js, commodity-label.js, action-prefix.js and copy/thousands-separators.js; copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js; and the two fit specs fit/consignment-details.fit.spec.js (547 lines, 6 describes, 24 tests) and fit/identification.fit.spec.js (1,460 lines, 9 describes, 42 tests including a 10-case identifier-length loop and a no-JavaScript describe). Read for context but left to part 9: features/commodities/view-model/selected-commodity-rows.js and commodity-groups.js (which build both pages' tables), commodity-question-detour.js, and check-answers/view-model/applicability.js (packagesApply). Covered: the consignment details page (slug consignment-details) with its caption, H1, selected-commodities table and columns, per-code group and per-species sub-headings, number of animals and number of packages fields, every validation message including the count-drop rule, both removal controls and where they lead, its save actions and persistence; the animal identification page (slug commodities/identification) with its inset, selected-commodities summary and Change link, Add another commodity link, per-code sections, per-species summary cards, the counter, the identifier fields asked of each commodity and species, the saved-animals table and its remove control, the in-card save buttons, the line cap and its wording, every identifier validation message, the per-card error summary, and the no-JavaScript behaviour; the display formatters (species label, commodity label, thousands separators, animal row label, total animals); and the Welsh key parity.

claims.statement: A commodity line counts as short of its identified animals when it is a commodity that is identified and the records holding at least one identifier are fewer than its number of animals.
claims.quote:
const isShortOfIdentifiedAnimals = (answers, evaluation, line) =>
  identifiedCommodityCodes().includes(line.entry.commodityCode) &&
  countOfIdentifiedAnimals(answers, evaluation, line) <
    Number(line.entry.numberOfAnimalsQuantity)
claims.note: mechanism: counts the identifier records of each commodity line. The confirmation feature reads it to say what is still outstanding.

claims.statement: The Welsh copy file carries the same key tree as the English one, with Welsh wording for every label, hint, button and error message both detail pages use.
The Welsh wording is a machine draft no translator has reviewed, and is marked as not to be shown to users without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.

claims.statement: The Welsh count-drop message does not singularise its counts the way the English one does: it reads "cofnod dynodwr" and "anifail" whatever the numbers are.
claims.quote:
countDrop: (records, species, entered) =>
        `Mae gennych ${records} cofnod dynodwr ar gyfer ${species} ond fe wnaethoch nodi ${entered} anifail. Tynnwch gofnodion dynodwr neu cadwch y cyfrif uwch.`
claims.note: Recorded as read; this part does not judge whether the Welsh form is right.

claims.statement: Nothing in these two pages limits how many commodity lines a notification may hold, or how many identifier records a line may hold beyond its own number of animals.
claims.note: Looked in both pages' validation (consignment-details/fields.js, consignment-details/validation/count-drop.js, animal-identification/identifier/fields.js) and in line-cap.js: the only numeric limits are the per-field maximum of 2147483647 and the per-line animal count. Any overall limit would sit in the set's limits doc or obligations, outside this part.

claims.statement: Neither page says what happens to a line's saved identifier records when its number of animals is raised rather than dropped.
claims.note: The count-drop rule only refuses a count below the records saved. Raising the count is accepted with no message, and this part holds no test for what the cards then show, beyond the counter reading the new cap.
